## Personality

Bright, bold and impatient, she wants to learn the exciting spells first and the listening never.

## Lore

Liri is nine years old, and she has decided that she has waited quite long enough. She is bright, bold and impatient, and she wants to learn the exciting spells first, the ones with light and noise and sparks, and the listening never. She has been at the Grove School for a year, which in her opinion is a year of sitting still that nobody will ever give back to her.

### The tea house girl

Liri was born in the forest and has lived all her life at the Dewdrop Tea House on the Lantern Paths, where her mother Tansy serves dew tea and honey cakes to everyone who passes. Her father, Edrin, kept the bees whose honey goes into those cakes; he died of a winter fever when she was one, and she does not remember him. She knows him from the hives her mother still tends and from the way some of the older guests look at her and say she has his chin.

Growing up in a tea house has taught Liri two things. The first is that if you sit quietly under a table, grown-ups forget you are there and say interesting things. The second is that the most interesting things are always about the roads: what travellers met on the way, which paths have turned bad, what the creatures beyond the Forest Edge look like now. Liri has heard a great many of these stories. She has never seen a monster, and it seems to her deeply unfair that she should live so close to them and never see one.

### School

Liri's teacher for the first and oldest lesson is Sorrel, who teaches listening: to trees, wind and creatures, before trying any magic at all. Sorrel's lessons are mostly silence. Liri finds silence unbearable. She likes Sorrel, which makes it worse, because she cannot even be properly cross with him. She has learned to sit still in his lessons for almost a quarter of an hour at a time, which he says is progress, and which she says is torture.

What she wants is to be like the wandering Magicians who come through the tea house with singed sleeves and stories, and to go out onto the roads herself one day and make them safe.

### Lumi

Her best friend is Lumi, one of the Children of the Tree, who joined the Grove School to learn the forest's ways. Lumi asks the questions nobody else dares to and laughs at most of the answers, and Liri thinks Lumi is the most interesting person she has ever met. They sit together in every lesson, share every honey cake, and get into trouble roughly once a week.

### The plan

Liri has a plan. She is going to sneak out to the Forest Edge, past the last lanterns, and see a real monster with her own eyes; only for a moment, she tells herself, and only from very far away. She has worked out when the edge watch changes, which path has the fewest lanterns, and how long she can be gone before her mother notices. She has told only Lumi.

She has not noticed that Lumi has been quiet about it lately, or that her mother has started watching her a little too carefully at supper. She is nine, and she is quite sure nobody suspects a thing.

### What she fears

Liri would never admit to being afraid of anything. But she is afraid, a little, of what her mother's face would look like if something went wrong, and she has not let herself think about that part of the plan for very long.

A quest might ask a traveller to keep an eye on the paths near the Edge on the night Liri chooses, to help Lumi decide whether to tell, or to find some safer way for a bold girl to see what she so badly wants to see.
